Just finished a Kafka collection. Who are your favorite short story authors, /v/Books?

Can't seem to include text in the post, so commenting instead.

This was my first intro to "sophisticated" short stories outside of one or two Asimov stories, and I'm hungry for more. Any recommendations?

I love short stories. And I've mostly been reading "mainstream lit" for the past couple of years.

There are a ton of wonderful "Great Short Stories" collections out there.

For classics, check collections edited by Milton Crane, Robert Penn Warren or Roger Goodman (should all be cheap) or others

Kafka, Chekhov, de Maupessant, Saki, Ring Lardner, Flanner O'Conner, John Cheever, Raymond Carver, John O'Hara, Dorothy Parker

For more contemporary stuff try "The Best Short Stories of xxxx" and pick a year. Anything over two or three years old should be available cheap. Or search for "contemporary" under short stories (The Oxford Book Of, The Vintage Book of, etc.)

Contemporary authors I like: George Saunders, Jennifer Egan, Joyce Carol Oates, Stuart Dybek, Deborah Eisenberg, Amy Hempel, Lorrie Moore, Alice Munro, Wells Tower

I've been working my way through various volumes of "The Best Short Stories of 20xx" and picking up collections by the authors I like best. George Saunders' "10th of December" is great if you're used to sci-fi. Jennifer Egan's "A Visit From The Goon Squad" is either a weird novel or a set of linked short stories, all different styles and all good, Oates' career-spanning "High Lonesome" is amazing.

I'm halfway through the collected short stories of Evelyn Waugh. Lots of good ones in there.

PG Wodehouse wrote a lot of good short stories, but I prefer him in novel form, where he has time to build things up a bit more.
I actually enjoy Stephen King's short stories more than his novels.
I guess it's due to where I grew up, but I'm always fond of Flannery O'Connor and William Faulkner.
kurt vonnegut's welcome to the monkey house. personal favorites are EPICAC, welcome to the monkeyhouse, and howard bergeron.
Mark Twain, The Invalid's Story will knock your socks off. Best part is that all of his stuff is available for free.
I really love H.P. Lovecraft. I know it's quite dated, but there's something about his style that really captures my imagination...

How short does a story have to be to be considered a "short story" for you? I ask simply because many of the older scifi things I read would probably be considered novellas and/or short stories by today's standards. Spider Robinson, Theodore Sturgeon, Alfred Bester, Heinlein, Asimov, Philip K Dick or pretty anyone else who cut their chops writing magazine fiction back in the day.

Alan Dean Foster penned one of my favorite short stories, "With Friends Like These..."

This question isn't within the scope of science, at least as it exists now. There is no way to accurately quantify a continuous (i.e. not discrete; analog, not digital) subjective experience like happiness between subjects.

It may be possible to relate a very limited definition of happiness to some aspect of the reward pathway using existing knowledge of that system and its relationship to reward associated with nicotine or cocaine (etc).
